title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed performance telemetry after last runtime upgrade, discussed network routing and VPC peering issues, and agreed tuning steps (batching/quantization) plus security doc exchange. Agreed next steps for network traces, repeat benchmark with KV cache warmed, and schedule canary for runtime rollback if stability issues persist.
next_steps: Luca to run full end-to-end network trace and share routing tables (due 2026-06-12)
Ethan to re-run nightly benchmark with KV cache warmed and upload results to shared sheet (due 2026-06-11)
Maria to share updated security questionnaire and SOC2 section (due 2026-06-12)
Schedule canary rollback test with on-call window next Tuesday (owner: Maria, due 2026-06-16)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-10 15:00 PDT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Moretti (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (Atlas Head of Platform), Ethan Ross (Atlas SRE), Sofia Marin (Atlas Security), Daniel Kim (Atlas Data Eng)

[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: we want to review the results from the upgrade over the weekend, check the VPC peering routing issue Ethan raised, and confirm next steps for tuning.
[00:18] Priya Patel: Yep, thanks Maria. We got reports of some 504s and a spike in tail latency saturday morning after you rolled the runtime.
[00:30] Luca Moretti: Right, that was the minor patch to the inference runtime to add improved kernel selection for long-context. We saw it shift some KV cache behavior. It should be a config togg-le, but we may have missed the default for cache warmup.
[00:46] Ethan Ross: The weirdness was intermittent, like a few requests timed out, then normal. I pulled a couple traces; some calls were getting routed to a standby node that hadn't pulled the quantized weights yet, so cold start + routing mismatch.
[01:05] Anika Rao: (quick) we also saw an uptick in token cost for a subset of calls, which I think is related.
[01:12] Maria Chen: Okay that's helpful. Luca, can you explain the fallback routing and the KV cache invalidation?
[01:20] Luca Moretti: Sure, so the change adjusted kernel selection heuristics; on longer sequences it prefers a different kernel that expects different memory layout. When a node restarts it rebuilds the KV cache. If the request routing policy hits a node that's still loading weights and the cache isn't populated, you get higher latency. There's also a small race where the routing health-checks passed but the model init wasn't finished.
[01:43] Priya Patel: So that explains the cold path. Is there a way to force warm-up or pin a canary pool until the nodes are fully loaded?
[01:51] Luca Moretti: Yes we have two options: 1) a pre-warm job that streams a representative set of prompts to build the KV stores, or 2) pinning canary nodes and only flip traffic after model-ready events. We recommend pre-warm for this pilot.
[02:12] Ethan Ross: We can run pre-warm, but need to ensure network egress and IAM roles are correct — some of our subnets block outbound initially.
[02:22] Maria Chen: Good point. Priya, what did you see on the peering front?
[02:28] Priya Patel: We noticed some asymmetric routing between the customer VPC and Redwood's peered VPC. On heavy load packets sometimes routed through a different AZ and hit an NACL that blocks ephemeral ports.
[02:42] Daniel Kim: I captured a pcap, looks like return path goes via transit gateway in us-west-2b then hits a stricter ACL on 1024-65535.
[02:55] Luca Moretti: That fits with the symptoms. We usually recommend allowing ephemeral ports and ensuring the transit gateway has consistent route propagation. Also check MTU mismatches; we had one case where fragmentation caused timeouts.
[03:08] Ethan Ross: We'll open a ticket on infra to relax the ephemeral ACL for the pilot subnets.
[03:12] Sofia Marin: From security perspective, we need to make sure flow logs and VPC logs are preserved for 90 days. Also want to confirm Redwood's audit trail for model access.
[03:24] Maria Chen: Yep, we can provide audit logs and the security questionnaire. I'll send the SOC2 extract.
[03:29] Priya Patel: That would be great. Also, can you confirm if keys are customer-managed for the private deployment?
[03:36] Luca Moretti: Yes, we support KMS integration; for on-prem customers you can bring your own HSM. For VPC pilots you'll likely use their KMS with cross-account permissions.
[03:46] Priya Patel: Perfect.
[03:48] Maria Chen: Back to the performance numbers, Anika — can you run through the dashboard highlights?
[03:53] Anika Rao: Sure. Overall  p50 is stable at ~170ms per token, p95 spiked to ~1.3s during the window. The spike aligns with the model init events. Throughput stayed within the SLA but we lost a few requests that hit the cold node and timed out after 10s. The token cost delta is about +6% for the affected windows.
[04:20] Daniel Kim: Are we seeing any correlation with sequence length? Our workload has a bimodal token distribution — short queries and some long context sessions.
[04:28] Anika Rao: Yes, the long-context flows are where the new kernel kicks in; those are the ones that saw the larger latency variance.
[04:35] Luca Moretti: So a mitigation plan: pin long-context traffic to a warm pool, run pre-warm job for the long-context model variant, and adjust routing so that new nodes don't receive traffic until model-ready.
[04:50] Ethan Ross: Routing change is doable but we'll need to coordinate with our networking team. Also, can we get a toggle in the control plane to disable the new kernel? If we need an immediate rollback.
[05:02] Maria Chen: We can flip runtime flags. Luca, how fast is rollback?
[05:07] Luca Moretti: We can push a config flip in under 5 minutes for a canary group; full fleet depends on scale but typically under 30 minutes. Rolling back the kernel selection is a config change, but nodes will still reload — which may cause another warmup window.
[05:22] Priya Patel: So we need to schedule a controlled rollback window if we do that.
[05:26] Maria Chen: Agreed. We'll plan a canary rollback test next Tuesday.
[05:31] Priya Patel: On the network side, we also found a suboptimal route advertised from our transit gw causing asymmetric return traffic. Ethan will share the routing table.
[05:42] Ethan Ross: I'll extract and share the route table and the traceroutes.
[05:45] Daniel Kim: Quick question on quantization — you mentioned quantized weights earlier, do we need to change our payload or is that transparent?
[05:52] Luca Moretti: Transparent to the client. The runtime loads quantized artifacts, but we need to ensure the node has the correct quantized model variant. If the node failed to fetch the artifact due to IAM issue you hit a cold path.
[06:06] Sofia Marin: For the security review, we also want to confirm access controls over model artifacts. Who has permission to push?
[06:13] Maria Chen: That goes through Redwood's model onboarding process; we'll share the model access ACL doc. We can gate artifact push to a small group and require signed manifests.
[06:23] Priya Patel: Good.
[06:25] Maria Chen: Any other blockers on your side for the tuning tasks?
[06:29] Ethan Ross: Main blocker is getting the VPC ephemeral ACL relaxed and confirming outbound access for the pre-warm job. Once that's done we'll re-run benchmarks.
[06:38] Priya Patel: Timeline wise, we want to decide go/no-go for prod by end of June; so we need these actions done this week.
[06:46] Maria Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize. Luca, can you propose a pre-warm job script that Ethan can run inside their VPC?
[06:55] Luca Moretti: Yes, I'll create a small script — it streams 500 representative prompts over 10 minutes to warm KV and confirm readiness. I'll post it in the shared drive.
[07:06] Daniel Kim: Please note the script needs to use our internal prompt set; I'll share that list.
[07:11] Maria Chen: Great. Anika, any notes on batching/quantization tuning?
[07:15] Anika Rao: For the pilot we recommend: conservative batching (max tokens 512, max batch size 8) for long-context, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and keep quantization at 8-bit for now. We'll run a short A/B: current config vs conservative batch to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:34] Priya Patel: If we lower batch size will that increase cost?
[07:38] Anika Rao: Slightly per-token cost may rise but p95 latency will improve. For production we'll tune for cost once traffic is stable.
[07:47] Maria Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll capture the token-level breakdown for the A/B.
[07:50] Ethan Ross: On the tooling side, can you push more verbose traces to our tracing endpoint so we can correlate request IDs? Last time some requests didn't have matching trace ids.
[07:59] Luca Moretti: Yes we can include request-id propagation headers; just confirm the collector endpoint.
[08:05] Priya Patel: We'll provide the collector endpoint and sample creds.
[08:09] Maria Chen: Ok wrapping up — let's recap action items. Luca will share the pre-warm script, collect VPC flow logs and run traceroutes. Ethan will rerun the benchmark with warmed cache and share route tables. Maria will send SOC2 excerpt and security docs and schedule the rollback canary next Tuesday. Priya will confirm stakeholders.
[08:30] Priya Patel: One last thing — can you share an estimated cost delta if we keep conservative batching for long-context? We need to show finance the delta.
[08:39] Anika Rao: I'll model a rough estimate in the shared spreadsheet and include both cost and p95 latency numbers.
[08:46] Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll sync mid-week if needed.
[08:50] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains a few transcription artifacts (e.g., "toggle" -> "togg-le", occasional speaker mislabels), timestamps approximate. References to docs: shared drive link to pre-warm script (link: drive.redwood/company/atlas/prewarm), security questionnaire (link: drive.redwood/security/atlas-sq.pdf), benchmark sheet (link: sheets.redwood/atlas-pilot).
